sections.h2: Will a fast sale work for a Pasadena home?
sections.html:
Yes. Pasadena sits in southeastern Harris County, and houses there sell by cash offer, investor purchase or agent listing. The fastest closings happen when the seller has the deed, a mortgage payoff figure and a tax certificate ready before the contract is signed.

What slows a Pasadena sale is usually not the buyer. It is a title problem, an unpaid tax year, a tenant, or heirs who have not agreed. This page covers the local picture, the Harris County tax steps a seller meets, and the situations that call for extra paperwork.

sections.h2: How did Pasadena grow into an industrial suburb?
sections.html:
Pasadena is an industrial suburb with a farming past. The Handbook of Texas entry, linked from the city's own site, says John H. Burnett of Galveston founded it in 1893 and named it after Pasadena, California. A rail line came through in 1894, and after the 1900 Galveston hurricane the area became a strawberry center for Gulf Coast farmers.

The economy changed in the late 1930s as ship channel industries grew. Pasadena had 3,436 residents in 1940 and 22,483 in 1950, and the city annexed Deepwater, Middle Bayou and Red Bluff. By 1980 it covered 58.6 square miles. Refineries, the Bayport industrial district and the Johnson Space Center in nearby Clear Lake are tied to local jobs.

Pasadena voted to incorporate in 1923, disincorporated in 1924, and voted again in 1928. The residents formed an independent school system in 1899, the first in Harris County, and the Pasadena district absorbed the Genoa and South Houston districts in 1935.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Pasadena house?
sections.html:
The Harris County Tax Office collects on Pasadena homes alongside the other units on the bill, and the Harris Central Appraisal District sets the values. The Comptroller's basics page describes an appraiser of record each January 1 that leaves rate setting to the taxing units.

The county's FAQ says statements are due on receipt and should be paid by January 31 of the next year. Pay by then and no penalty or interest is added. Request a statement from the tax office before you take an offer, so the figure in your contract matches the county's record.

sections.h2: What do Harris County's penalty and payment rules look like?
sections.html:
The table summarizes what the Harris County Tax Office prints on its FAQ page. Check the live page for the current year before relying on a date.

Harris County Tax Office property tax rules from its FAQ
TopicWhat the office prints
Timely paymentDue by January 31 of the following year
Late month-one charge6% penalty and 1% interest for February
Homestead installment plans12 to 36 months available
Plan start for current-year delinquencyFirst business day in February
Referral to a collection law firmAdditional 15% to 20% penalty on the balance
Tax salesHeld by the eight county constables

A seller whose taxes are behind can pay them from closing proceeds, so a delinquency does not by itself block a sale. It does raise the payoff, so ask for a figure dated for your closing day.

sections.h2: What payment plans does Harris County describe for late taxes?
sections.html:
Harris County's FAQ lays out several ways to catch up. A homestead owner can enter an installment agreement at any time once taxes are delinquent, and current-year agreements open on the first business day of February. The county says requests are accepted after January 31 and before March 1, with the 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest assessed for February.

  • Payment plans run from 12 months up to 36 months for homestead property.
  • A deferral can protect the amount owed, but interest of 5 percent per year is added for each year taxes stay delinquent.
  • Online and phone payments count if completed by 11:59 p.m. on or before the due date.
  • Mail must be postmarked on or before the due date.

A seller planning to move can use a plan to buy time, then pay the balance from closing proceeds.

sections.h2: How do taxes get handled at a Pasadena closing?
sections.html:
The title company asks for a tax certificate showing what is paid, and any unpaid amount comes out of your proceeds. The county FAQ warns about one timing trap: a closing between November 15 and January 31 on a mortgage that escrows taxes. If that is you, call the lender once the date is set so the bill is paid and the certificate is clean.

  • Tell the title company if the lender paid this year's bill from escrow.
  • Ask for any escrow balance back after the payoff.
  • If you claimed a homestead exemption and then sold, the county asks you to correct the account.

Taxes that stay unpaid keep a lien on the property, so the buyer's title will not be clear until they are paid.

sections.h2: What exemptions and caps should a Pasadena owner check before selling?
sections.html:
Exemptions shape the bill the next owner will see. The Comptroller says school districts must grant a $140,000 homestead exemption, with a further $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.

  • Homestead value growth is capped at 10 percent a year.
  • Disabled veterans may get $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a 100 percent rating can mean a full exemption.
  • A late-year buyer may claim the exemption for the rest of that year if you never did.

Several taxing units can sit on one Pasadena bill, so look at every line.

sections.h2: What if the Pasadena house has a tenant or a tax judgment?
sections.html:
A sale is still possible, and each case has its own Texas procedure.

  • Tenant. An eviction begins with written notice to vacate and a justice court case, and a writ of possession is available six days after a final judgment. A buyer will ask for the lease and deposit details.
  • Tax judgment. Harris County says the eight constables hold the tax sales for property taken to judgment, buyers take the property as is, and sales are final.
  • Collection firm. Accounts sent to a law firm face a further 15 to 20 percent penalty.

Clearing the tax before it reaches judgment keeps more of your proceeds. Call the county at the number on its site for a payoff.

sections.h2: Which Pasadena facts help describe the house to buyers?
sections.html:
Buyers care about commute, schools and employers. The state history handbook says employment is tied to ship channel industries, the Bayport Industrial District and the Johnson Space Center in nearby Clear Lake. San Jacinto College and Texas Chiropractic College are in Pasadena.

  • Pasadena runs its own school district, begun in 1899.
  • The city grew from 1.7 square miles in 1893 to 58.6 square miles in 1980.
  • The Pasadena Rodeo and San Jacinto Strawberry Festival are listed as major draws.

Mention which of these a house is close to when you talk with a buyer.

faqs.q: Which county bills Pasadena property tax?
faqs.a: Harris County. Its tax office collects, and the Harris Central Appraisal District sets values. Ask for a payoff and a certificate before closing.

faqs.q: Must I clear delinquent taxes before selling?
faqs.a: No. They can be paid from proceeds at closing, though penalty and interest grow, so request a figure dated for the closing day.

faqs.q: When is the county's tax deadline?
faqs.a: January 31 of the year after the tax year, per the Harris County FAQ. Payment by then carries no penalty or interest.

faqs.q: What happens to my escrow if I sell in winter?
faqs.a: Your lender may have paid the bill already. Give it the closing date promptly and ask for any balance after payoff.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a tenant in place?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes it subject to the lease, unless you follow the Texas notice and court steps to clear the house first.
